children: Institutional investment in Indian real estate reached $1.42 billion in Q3 2026, with domestic investors accounting for 65% of quarterly inflows

Private equity investment in Indian real estate rose 39 per cent year-on-year to USD 5.93 billion during January-September 2026, compared with USD 4.27 billion in the corresponding period last year, according to data compiled by Colliers.

Investment inflows during the third quarter of 2026 stood at USD 1.42 billion, up 12 per cent from USD 1.27 billion in Q3 2025. Multi-city and other markets accounted for the largest share of quarterly investment, attracting USD 860.4 million or 61 per cent of total inflows.

Domestic investors continued to dominate institutional investment activity during the quarter, contributing USD 926.3 million, or 65 per cent of total Q3 inflows. Foreign investors accounted for USD 490 million, representing the remaining 35 per cent.

On a year-to-date basis, domestic investment rose 59 per cent to USD 3.49 billion, giving domestic investors a 59 per cent share of total institutional inflows. Foreign investment increased 17 per cent to USD 2.44 billion and accounted for 41 per cent of the YTD total.
Delhi NCR, Mumbai Lead Major Cities

Delhi NCR recorded a sharp increase in investment inflows during Q3, rising 438 per cent year-on-year to USD 157.1 million from USD 29.2 million. Mumbai attracted USD 240.2 million, up 57 per cent from USD 153.2 million a year earlier.

Pune recorded USD 105.1 million in Q3 investment, although this was 62 per cent lower than the year-ago period. Bengaluru saw inflows decline 7 per cent to USD 29 million, while Chennai recorded a steep 91 per cent decline to USD 24.5 million.

For the first nine months of 2026, Bengaluru led among the major cities with USD 643.4 million, followed by Chennai at USD 639.4 million and Delhi NCR at USD 581.7 million. However, the largest share came from other and multi-city investments, which totalled USD 2.94 billion, up 125 per cent year-on-year.
Hospitality Emerges As Key Investment Theme

Hospitality accounted for 25 per cent of total real estate investment inflows in Q3 2026, making it the largest asset class during the quarter. Office assets followed with a 20 per cent share, while residential accounted for 16 per cent.

Industrial and warehousing assets attracted 13 per cent of quarterly inflows, alternatives accounted for 14 per cent and mixed-use assets for 12 per cent. Retail investment was negligible during the quarter.

For January-September 2026, office remained the dominant asset class, accounting for 37 per cent of total investment. Mixed-use assets accounted for 17 per cent, alternatives 16 per cent, residential 12 per cent and hospitality 11 per cent.

Among select Q3 transactions, Canada Pension Plan Investment Board’s investment in Prestige Hospitality Ventures Ltd, the hospitality platform of Prestige Estates Projects, was the largest at USD 312 million.

Brookfield India Real Estate Trust and Prime Offices Fund invested USD 178.2 million in office assets in Mumbai. Kotak Realty Fund invested USD 83.7 million in Smartworld Developers in the Delhi-NCR residential market, while ASK Property Fund invested USD 31.8 million in BRV Group and KW Group. Certus Capital invested USD 28.5 million in 4S Developers.

The largest transaction recorded during January-September 2026 was a USD 675 million investment by Abu Dhabi Investment Authority in Kotak Alternate Asset Managers in Q2, followed by CPPIB’s USD 440 million investment in Ctrl S.

Overall, the data points to continued institutional appetite for Indian real estate, with domestic capital playing an increasingly important role and multi-city transactions accounting for a significant portion of investment activity.
